message.content:
Update these two files to reflect the expanded 18-category taxonomy for the Unearth web discovery platform. The previous taxonomy had 11 categories; it now has 18 with 108 subcategories.

The 7 new parent categories are:
- Sports & Athletics (`sports-athletics`) ⚽ — Team Sports, Individual Sports, Combat & Martial Arts, Outdoor & Adventure Sports, Fantasy & Sports Analytics, Fitness & Training
- Finance & Money (`finance-money`) 💰 — Personal Finance, Investing, Crypto & Web3, Economics, Financial Tools, Real Estate
- News & Current Events (`news-current-events`) 🌍 — World Affairs, Politics & Policy, Business & Market News, Science & Tech News, Local & Community News
- Humor & Entertainment (`humor-entertainment`) 😂 — Comedy & Satire, Pop Culture, Memes & Internet Humor, Reviews & Criticism, Quizzes & Fun
- Pets & Animals (`pets-animals`) 🐾 — Dogs, Cats, Exotic & Unusual Pets, Wildlife & Conservation, Veterinary & Pet Health
- Parenting & Family (`parenting-family`) 👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 — Baby & Toddler, Kids Activities & Education, Teen & Tween, Family Life, Pregnancy & Fertility
- Automotive & Transport (`automotive-transport`) 🚗 — Electric Vehicles, Cars & Trucks, Motorcycles, Aviation & Space Vehicles, Future of Transport

Also: "Fitness & Health" was moved from Lifestyle & Wellness to Sports & Athletics as "Fitness & Training". "Mindfulness & Spirituality" was added to Lifestyle & Wellness.

FILES TO UPDATE:

1. /sessions/clever-nice-ptolemy/mnt/outputs/skills/content-pipeline/references/taxonomy.md — Update the taxonomy structure listing and all rules to reference 18 parents

2. /sessions/clever-nice-ptolemy/mnt/outputs/skills/supabase-schema/references/taxonomy-seed.md — Add SQL INSERT statements for all 7 new parent categories and their subcategories, following the exact same CROSS JOIN pattern used for existing categories. Also update the Lifestyle & Wellness subcategories (remove Fitness & Health, add Mindfulness & Spirituality).

Read both files first, then update them.

     2→
     3→This is the controlled category taxonomy for Unearth. Categories are organized in a two-level hierarchy: 11 parent categories with 5–6 subcategories each (66 total).
     4→
     5→## UX Behavior
     6→
     7→Selecting a parent = all children enabled. Users can then uncheck individual subcategories. Partial selection shows indeterminate state on parent. Minimum 3 parents selected during onboarding.

    94→- Communities & Networking (`communities`)
    95→- Personal Branding (`personal-branding`)
    96→
    97→## Taxonomy Rules
    98→
    99→1. Every site gets 2–3 subcategory slugs (primary + secondary)
   100→2. Sites also get 5–10 freeform tags for more specific matching (e.g., "react", "css-animation", "postgres")
   101→3. The taxonomy can expand over time but changes should be deliberate — new subcategories require updating the interests table and retagging affected sites
   102→4. When the AI tagger suggests a category not in the taxonomy, flag it for review rather than auto-creating
   103→5. A site can span multiple parent categories (e.g., a design tool startup might be tagged `ui-ux` + `saas-products`)
   104→
   105→## Pack Generation Rules
   106→
   107→1. Match sites to user's enabled subcategories
   108→2. Weight toward subcategories where user has kept more cards
   109→3. Max 2 cards from the same parent category per pack
   110→4. Never show a site the user has already seen
   111→5. 1 of 5 cards should be a "serendipity pick" from outside selected interests
   112→6. Quality floor: only sites scoring ≥ 70 appear in standard packs
   113→

   156→
   157→## Storing User Interest Selections
   158→
   159→User interest selections are stored as an array of subcategory slugs on the `profiles` table:
   160→
   161→```sql
   162→-- Example: user selected all of Technology + some Design subcategories
   163→UPDATE profiles SET interests = ARRAY[
   164→  'ai-ml', 'developer-tools', 'new-products', 'open-source', 'cybersecurity-privacy', 'mobile-apps',
   165→  'web-design', 'ui-ux', 'graphic-design'
   166→] WHERE id = 'user-uuid';
   167→```
   168→
   169→The array stores **subcategory slugs only**. Parent categories are inferred by checking if all children of a parent are present in the array. This keeps the data model flat while supporting the parent/child checkbox UI.

   243→## Storing User Interest Selections
   244→
   245→User interest selections are stored as an array of subcategory slugs on the `profiles` table:
   246→
   247→```sql
   248→-- Example: user selected all of Technology + some Design subcategories
   249→UPDATE profiles SET interests = ARRAY[
   250→  'ai-ml', 'developer-tools', 'new-products', 'open-source', 'cybersecurity-privacy', 'mobile-apps',
   251→  'web-design', 'ui-ux', 'graphic-design'
   252→] WHERE id = 'user-uuid';
   253→```
   254→
   255→The array stores **subcategory slugs only**. Parent categories are inferred by checking if all children of a parent are present in the array. This keeps the data model flat while supporting the parent/child checkbox UI.
